rules.title: Newark rent control limits on excessive rents, hardship increases, utility surcharges, and rent decreases
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge rent above the amount received on the chapter’s effective date unless the increase is authorized by the Newark rent control chapter. Hardship increases are limited to once in any 12-month period, utility surcharges require documented heating or water expense increases over 10% and are capped by building size, and tenants may petition for rent decreases when services are reduced.
rules.key_value: Unauthorized increases barred; hardship increases no more than once per 12 months; utility surcharge caps of 15%, 5%, or 3% of monthly rent roll depending on unit count

coverage.summary: The excerpt refers to rental units, dwellings, apartments, and tenants subject to the Newark rent control chapter, but does not state the chapter’s full coverage or exemptions.

rules.exemptions: No attorney's fees, accountant's fees or application fees incurred by a landlord in connection with an application to the Board may be included in determining whether the landlord is entitled to rent increases.
rules.penalty: The Rent Control Board may impose a monetary penalty not to exceed $500 for a violation of any provision of the chapter, after notice and an opportunity for hearing.
rules.interaction: The excerpt says rent above the chapter’s baseline is allowed only for increases authorized by the Newark rent control chapter, and hardship increases require substantial compliance with State and Newark codes.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall after the effective date of this chapter charge any rents in excess of what he/she was receiving from the effective date of this chapter except for increases authorized by this chapter.

rules.law_name: Newark Rent Control Regulations Retaliatory Eviction and Protected Tenancy Provisions
rules.title: Protection from retaliatory eviction and condo/co-op conversion eviction for eligible senior and disabled tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession as retaliation for a tenant’s effort to secure or enforce rights under the Newark rent control chapter. The ordinance also provides an application process for senior citizen and disabled tenants seeking protected tenancy status from eviction due to condominium or cooperative conversion.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Protected tenancy for condominium or cooperative conversion depends on senior citizen or disabled tenant eligibility standards under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22.
coverage.summary: The retaliatory-eviction ban applies to dwelling units under the Newark rent control chapter; the protected-tenancy provision applies to eligible senior citizen or disabled tenants facing eviction from condominium or cooperative conversions.

rules.penalty: The Rent Control Board may impose a monetary penalty not to exceed $500 for a violation of any provision of the chapter, after notice and an opportunity for hearing.
rules.interaction: The protected-tenancy provision states that eligibility determinations are guided by the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
